command: llvm-mc -triple=x86_64 -filetype=obj X86-P75-sse-riprel32.s -o out.o && llvm-objcopy -O binary --only-section=.text out.o out.bin
notes: Input, one line each (LF, trailing newline): `movaps L1(%rip), %xmm0` / `movaps %xmm0, L1(%rip)` / `vmovaps L1(%rip), %xmm0` / `vmovaps %xmm0, L1(%rip)` / `{evex} vmovaps L1(%rip), %xmm0` / `{evex} vmovaps %xmm0, L1(%rip)` / `.space 16` / `L1:` / `.byte 0xaa, 0xbb, 0xcc, 0xdd`. The six instructions are 7/7/8/8/10/10 bytes, so `L1` at offset 66 gives the displacements 59/52/44/36/26/16. The plan states the same bytes through six `pcrel_end` fixups whose `field_descriptor` is `[24,32]` for the legacy pair, `[32,32]` for the VEX pair and `[48,32]` for the EVEX pair; all use `resolve_in_place`, so no relocation record is emitted and `records` is 0.
source: `llvm-mc` 23.1.2 selection plus the `mod = 00`, `r/m = 101` rule already pinned by `EC-34`; the displacement is measured from the end of the instruction (`03_fixup_model.md` §4, `pcrel_end`)
